objectives.text: Get back an elected government. The Transitional Presidential Council, formed in April 2024 to hold power until an election or 7 February 2026, dissolved on that date with no presidential election held and no successor structure agreed. The prime minister, Alix Didier Fils-Aime, governs with the backing of Washington, which threatened 'serious consequences' against any move to oust him. No election date was found in sources.

objectives.text: Retake Port-au-Prince from the gang coalition Viv Ansanm with a foreign force, the Gang Suppression Force (GSF), authorised by the Security Council at up to 5,550 personnel. About 1,500 troops were in place when the mandate was renewed on 29 September 2026, and the Kenyan contingent is being replaced by Chadian troops.

means.text: A foreign-manned force, not a Haitian one: the GSF works with the Haitian National Police and the Armed Forces of Haiti. Personnel were pledged by Kenya (until its exit), Chad, Jamaica, the Bahamas, Guyana, Barbados, Antigua and Barbuda, Bangladesh and Benin. Pledges are not deployments; the troops in place are about 1,500.

constraints.text: The force is funded and staffed below plan and its contributors are leaving: Kenya brought its second contingent home in March 2026 and Chad is replacing it. Haiti's own police cannot yet hold the ground the force takes.

paradoxes.text: The foreign force that keeps the capital from falling to the gangs also keeps the Haitian police and army from being rebuilt, since the GSF is the security. When the contributors leave, the gap returns to the streets; the security bought from outside is what makes the interim survivable, and the interim is what should have built Haitian security.

grand_strategy.reading: Haiti's grand strategy is to get back an elected government and to retake Port-au-Prince, and it pays for both by renting its security from a UN-authorised foreign force (Kenya first, now Chad and others) and by living on remittances that tie it to its diaspora and to the United States. The transition ended on 7 February 2026 without an election or a successor, and the prime minister now governs on Washington's backing, while the force holds about a quarter of its authorised strength and its own police are not yet rebuilt. Not verified for this card: cholera and famine, which were asked for as constraints but for which no source was reached within the budget, the CARICOM mediation, the OAS and UN positions beyond the mission, and the Dominican wall.

stances.note: Viv Ansanm, formed in September 2023 by G9 and G-Pèp, was created to attack the Haitian government (police stations, government buildings, infrastructure) and to fight the international force (Wikipedia, tier 4). Adversary is our reading, not a source's word, and it is the rare grade by design: the sources show hostile attacks on the state, not a stated aim of replacing it, so if a stricter reading is taken this becomes rival. Bond none: no kinship or affinity is named. Trend stable: the 2026 coverage shows continued killings, with no sign of a turn.

stances.note: Mirror of the KEN card's stance toward HTI (same sources, read from Haiti's side). Kenya led the Multinational Security Support mission from June 2024 and the Security Council turned it into the Gang Suppression Force on 30 September 2025; the Haitian state receives Kenyan police, and Kenya's second contingent came home in March 2026 with Chad replacing it. Partner and not ally: a service to the Haitian state, not an alliance. Cooling because the mission is winding down, with Haitian protests against the Kenyan exit reported in April 2026. Confidence C: this is our reading of the structure; the departure status after April 2026 is unconfirmed. Bond none.

stances.note: Washington is the patron of the post-transition arrangement: it backed Prime Minister Fils-Aime staying on after the council's mandate ended on 7 February 2026, threatened serious consequences against any removal and sanctioned five council members (Reuters, via Citizen Digital). Its funding of the force is not confirmed by any source reached here, so it is not stated. It is the major trading partner under HOPE and HELP (Wikipedia). Cooling is our reading from the 2026 terminations: the US has moved to end Temporary Protected Status for Haitians, and the Supreme Court in June 2026 let the termination for Haiti proceed (Wikipedia, tier 4). Partner, not ally: transactional and interest-based. Bond none: no source names a kinship or an open wound between the pair. The since date is the 2026 backing; the trade partnership is older. Confidence C.

stances.note: Relations have long been hostile: since Haiti's independence in 1804 the two states have had wars, massacres, border disputes and stand-offs, and migration keeps tension high in the 21st century (Wikipedia, tier 4). Rival is our reading: the sources show friction and no declared aim of destroying the other state. Bond grievance: the historical wounds are open and the migration dispute is ongoing. The Dominican Republic's measures against Haitian migrants are the current friction; the card does not assess them further, and the DOM card is in progress and not read here. Trend stable is provisional. Confidence C.

stances_toward.note: Our reading (C). Santo Domingo cooperates in the Haitian security mission (the Dominican foreign minister announced the Chadian rotation that replaces the Kenyan force) while resisting alignment with Haiti's state: the April 2025 package adds a 1,500-soldier border reinforcement, an accelerated wall and tougher penalties for migrant smugglers. The grade is reluctant_partner, not rival, because no source read calls the relation hostile. Trend cooling: the border measures harden over 2025-26. Bond grievance is our reading and stays unsourced for now: the historical wound between the two states is not in any source read yet, so it needs a source before the bond is treated as confirmed.

stances_toward.note: Kenya led the Multinational Security Support mission from the first police deployment in June 2024; the Security Council transformed it into the Gang Suppression Force (up to 5,550 personnel) on 30 September 2025, renewed it for six months on 29 September 2026 (12-0, China, Russia and Pakistan abstaining) with about 1,500 troops in place against 5,550 authorised. Kenya sent a fifth contingent of 230 officers in December 2025 (over 700 in all), brought the second contingent home on 17-18 March 2026 and is replaced gradually by Chadian troops trained in the US (Dominican Republic foreign minister, 2026). Partner and not ally: a service to the Haitian state and to Washington, not an alliance. Cooling because the mission is winding down, funded and staffed below plan, with Haitian protests against the Kenyan exit reported in April 2026 (People Daily). Confidence C: the departure status after April 2026 is unconfirmed. Bond none.
